hook.line: Four amazons each, White and Black. Every move and every arrow makes the board a little smaller.
hook.say: Welcome! Let me show you the story of Amazons.

ch.say: Born in 1988 — it's still a young game!
p: Amazons was invented in 1988 by Walter Zamkauskas of Argentina. It first appeared, in Spanish, in the Argentine puzzle magazine El Acertijo in December 1992.

In January 1994 Michael Keller's English translation appeared in World Game Review, and that same year Keller wrote the first computer version. Since 2000 it has been an event at the Computer Olympiad, where programs from around the world compete.

ch.say: Two things in one move — that's the key!
ch.cap: The 10×10 board: a white amazon moves from d1 to d7 and shoots an arrow to g7
p: An amazon moves like a chess queen: any distance along a row, column or diagonal (it can't pass amazons or arrows). Then, from where it lands, it shoots one arrow the same way, blocking that square.
A square with an arrow can never be used again. If none of your amazons can move on your turn, you lose. There are no draws.
